main_text.l: degunt: ut, pisces, catus, canis marinus, porcus ma-
rinus, &c.
Hisce addantur Amphibia, animantia in aquis &
terris degentia: ut, cancri, lutrae, Otter [?], &c.
Substantia sentiens rationalis est quae ratione prae-
dita est, ut Homo, creaturarum omnium nobilissimus.
Quaedam qualitates percipiuntur tactu, ut, Calor,
Frigus, Humor, Siccitas.
Quaedam percipiuntur visu, ut Lux & Color.
Quaedam qualitas sentitur gustu, ut sapor laxans
& astringens.
Sapor laxans est in lacte, vino dulci, melle, sacha-
ro, oleo, butyro carne.
Sapor astringens est in pipere, zingibere, allio, cep-
a, sale, pomis, pyris & prunis sylvestribus vino au-
stero, acetosa, saurampffer [?] / malo punico, grauat-
apffel/aceto, bile, absinthio.
Quaedam qualitas sentitur odoratu, ut odor bo-
nus, vel malus.
Odor bonus, ex rosa, viola, rosmarino provenit.
Odor malus ex cadavere, coeno, &c.
Quaedam qualitas sentitur auditu, ut sonus acu-
tus vel gravis.
Qui praecepta noscere cupiunt prolixiora, videant
solertissimi viri Domini Doctoris Scribonij Physi-
cam, cujus axiomata plaeraq; transcripsimus: Physi-
cam Domini Philippi Melanchthonis, ejusq; libel-
lum de Anima: Physicam Doctoris Thomae Frcigii.
Et Herbaria, quae a Doctis viris scripta passim extant.
Hactenus Physica expofita est: ubi autem definit
Physicus, ibi incipit Medicus: Recte igitur sequitur
Medicina.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Otter" appears to be black letter and its letters are uncertain. "saurampffer" is uncertain at the first letter and the ff ligature. "Frcigii" is printed as shown; the name is probably Freigii, but the scan reads Frcigii. The line-end hyphen in "grauat-apffel" is printed as a small mark and was read as a hyphen. The p in "plaeraq;" and the spelling "Physicam" are as printed. The page number 347 is printed with an unclear final digit that reads as 7.
